title: iOS: MetalFX is reported as unsupported on device because the exported Xcode project does not link MetalFX.framework
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (official) [ed1daf0bf]
- Not tested on device: 4.6.x and master. On master ([12c17c187](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/12c17c187e88efa23e6bbd6689630e256eca6523), 2026-10-01) the code involved is unchanged: neither the Xcode template nor the iOS exporter adds MetalFX.
- Probably a regression from #114484 (see "Regression" below).

### System information

iOS 26.6.2 - iPhone 17 Pro (iPhone18,1), Apple A19 Pro GPU (Apple9) - Godot v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] - Metal 4.0 (Mobile and Forward+) - exported on macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M5 Max) with Xcode 27.0 (27A266a)

### Issue description

In an iOS export, `RenderingDevice.has_feature(RenderingDevice.SUPPORTS_METALFX_SPATIAL)` and `has_feature(RenderingDevice.SUPPORTS_METALFX_TEMPORAL)` both return `false` on an iPhone 17 Pro (A19 Pro), which supports MetalFX. MetalFX Spatial then falls back to FSR, and MetalFX Temporal (Forward+) to FSR 2, with a warning that MetalFX is not supported "by the current renderer or hardware" ([renderer_viewport.cpp#L168-L184](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/servers/rendering/renderer_viewport.cpp#L168-L184)).

After adding `-framework MetalFX` to the exported Xcode project's linker flags, both return `true` on the same device, with both the Mobile and Forward+ renderers. Running the same project from the macOS editor (Apple M5 Max) prints `true` for both without changes.

**Cause**

- Since 4.7 the Metal driver uses metal-cpp. [metal_device_properties.cpp#L181-L187](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/drivers/metal/metal_device_properties.cpp#L181-L187) sets both features from `MTLFX::SpatialScalerDescriptor::supportsDevice()` and `MTLFX::TemporalScalerDescriptor::supportsDevice()`.
- metal-cpp does not reference the MetalFX classes at link time. It looks them up by name with `objc_lookUpClass()` in static initializers ([MTLFXPrivate.hpp#L54](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/thirdparty/metal-cpp/MetalFX/MTLFXPrivate.hpp#L54), [#L121-L122](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/thirdparty/metal-cpp/MetalFX/MTLFXPrivate.hpp#L121-L122)). If MetalFX.framework is not loaded, the class pointer is null and `supportsDevice()` returns `false` through `sendMessageSafe()` ([MTLFXSpatialScaler.hpp#L245-L248](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/thirdparty/metal-cpp/MetalFX/MTLFXSpatialScaler.hpp#L245-L248), [NSObject.hpp#L239-L250](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/thirdparty/metal-cpp/Foundation/NSObject.hpp#L239-L250)). Nothing fails at link time.
- macOS links MetalFX explicitly ([platform/macos/detect.py#L313-L317](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/platform/macos/detect.py#L313-L317)). Both the 4.7.2 editor and the 4.7.2 macOS release template list `MetalFX.framework` in `otool -L`.
- On iOS, nothing adds it:
  - `platform/ios/detect.py` only adds the header path ([#L160-L168](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/platform/ios/detect.py#L160-L168)).
  - The Xcode template's Frameworks phase and `OTHER_LDFLAGS` don't list it ([project.pbxproj#L59-L69](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/misc/dist/apple_embedded_xcode/godot_apple_embedded.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj#L59-L69), [#L266](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/misc/dist/apple_embedded_xcode/godot_apple_embedded.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj#L266)).
  - The exporter only adds linker flags that come from export plugins and `.gdip` plugins ([editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp#L757-L772](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/export/editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp#L757-L772), [#L1628-L1646](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/export/editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp#L1628-L1646)).
  - The autolink (`LC_LINKER_OPTION`) entries in the 4.7.2 `libgodot.ios.release.xcframework/ios-arm64/libgodot.a` name Metal, QuartzCore, UIKit and others, but not MetalFX.

  As exported, `otool -L` on the built app lists `Metal.framework` but not `MetalFX.framework`.

The metal-cpp behavior can also be checked on macOS. A small program built against the 4.7.2 `thirdparty/metal-cpp` calls the same two functions on an M5 Max:
- Without `-framework MetalFX`, `MTLFX::Private::Class::s_kMTLFXSpatialScalerDescriptor` is null and both calls return `false`.
- With `-framework MetalFX`, both return `true`.
- Calling `dlopen()` on MetalFX at the start of `main()` doesn't help: `objc_lookUpClass()` then finds the class, but metal-cpp has already cached the null pointer.

**Regression**

In 4.6.3 the driver was Objective-C++ and messaged `MTLFXSpatialScalerDescriptor` directly ([metal_device_properties.mm#L177-L179](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6.3-stable/drivers/metal/metal_device_properties.mm#L177-L179)), so MetalFX had to be linked for an iOS export to link at all. #101585 is the 4.4 link error when it wasn't. It was fixed by #101614, which weak-linked MetalFX in the iOS Xcode template; the current template no longer has that entry. #114484 replaced this code with metal-cpp's runtime lookup. Since then nothing needs or adds MetalFX on iOS, and the missing framework shows up as `false` at runtime instead of a link error.

Notes for a fix:
- The default minimum iOS version is 15.0 ([export_plugin.h#L44](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/platform/ios/export/export_plugin.h#L44)), and MetalFX requires iOS 16.0. So MetalFX probably needs to be weak-linked again, as #101614 did.
- The open metal-cpp upgrade #119582 references `OBJC_CLASS_$_MTLFX...` symbols directly. With it, the missing framework would likely become a link error on iOS.

Workaround (tested): add `-framework MetalFX` to `OTHER_LDFLAGS` of the exported project, for example `xcodebuild ... OTHER_LDFLAGS='$(inherited) -framework MetalFX'`. If the minimum iOS version is below 16.0, use `-weak_framework MetalFX` instead. That produces `LC_LOAD_WEAK_DYLIB` but was not tested on device.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP and export it for iOS as an Xcode project, with the default renderer (Mobile) and driver (Metal).
2. Build and run it on a device that supports MetalFX. The MRP enables file logging, so the output can be read from the app container:
   `xcrun devicectl device copy from --device <UDID> --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier <bundle id> --source Documents/logs/godot.log --destination godot.log`
   Both `SUPPORTS_METALFX_*` lines print `false`.
3. `otool -L <App>.app/<App> | grep MetalFX` prints nothing.
4. Build again with `OTHER_LDFLAGS='$(inherited) -framework MetalFX'`, for example on the `xcodebuild` command line, and run it. Both lines print `true`.

Note: the device results above (both `false` as exported, both `true` with `-framework MetalFX`) were observed on an iPhone 17 Pro in a larger project that runs these same two `has_feature()` checks at startup. The MRP below was verified on macOS and by inspecting its unsigned iOS build with `otool -L`.

For comparison, running the MRP from the macOS editor prints:

```
Godot 4.7.2-stable (official)
macOS 26.6.2, model Mac17,6
Renderer mobile, driver metal, GPU Apple M5 Max (Apple9)
SUPPORTS_METALFX_SPATIAL = true
SUPPORTS_METALFX_TEMPORAL = true
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

An empty project with a `Node3D` main scene running this script, with `debug/file_logging/enable_file_logging` and ETC2/ASTC texture import enabled (I can attach a zipped project if useful):

```gdscript
extends Node3D


func _ready() -> void:
	var rd := RenderingServer.get_rendering_device()
	print("Godot ", Engine.get_version_info().string)
	print(OS.get_name(), " ", OS.get_version(), ", model ", OS.get_model_name())
	print("Renderer ", RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method(),
			", driver ", RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_driver_name(),
			", GPU ", RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name())
	print("SUPPORTS_METALFX_SPATIAL = ", rd.has_feature(RenderingDevice.SUPPORTS_METALFX_SPATIAL))
	print("SUPPORTS_METALFX_TEMPORAL = ", rd.has_feature(RenderingDevice.SUPPORTS_METALFX_TEMPORAL))

	# Ask for MetalFX Spatial scaling so the renderer's fallback (if any) is logged.
	var cam := Camera3D.new()
	cam.position.z = 3.0
	add_child(cam)
	var box := MeshInstance3D.new()
	box.mesh = BoxMesh.new()
	add_child(box)
	get_viewport().scaling_3d_scale = 0.5
	get_viewport().scaling_3d_mode = Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_METALFX_SPATIAL

	if OS.has_feature("pc"):
		await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout
		get_tree().quit()
```
